agent-window.description: IPC for the detached AI chat window (label `agent`). It runs our own frontend bundle, so it gets the same core IPC as the main webview; browser-* windows (remote content) still match no capability at all.

browserbar.description: The chrome bar of the detached browser window (label `browserbar`, our own bundle, a child webview of `browserwin` beside the browser-N tabs). Authorised by its exact label: a webview holding remote content is always browser-* or reader and never matches. Tauri's ACL does not constrain an application's own custom commands one by one, so the allowlist below is a discipline list rather than an enforced boundary — what the bar actually calls is: browserbar_to_main / browserbar_set_expanded / browser_set_docked / browser_navigate / browser_open / browser_activate / browser_close_tab / browser_back / browser_forward / browser_reload / browser_focus / browser_state / bookmark_toggle / bookmark_list / vault_current / vault_last / notes_list / query_blocks / note_create / clips_lookup / settings_get. start-dragging: the bar's tab strip is the detached window's drag region.

capture-window.description: IPC for the quick capture window (label `capture`). It runs our own frontend bundle, matched exactly on that label like the chat window; browser-* windows (remote content) still match no capability at all. What it actually calls: capture_window_ready / capture_window_hide / capture_window_resize / capture_to_main / vault_current / notes_list / folders_list / files_list / privacy_list / query_blocks / note_create / attachment_save / files_import / clipboard_probe / clipboard_image / settings_get.

default.description: Default capability for the main window's own webview. Scoped to webviews (not windows) so any future webview attached to the main window does NOT inherit IPC — and browser-* windows never match at all.
